name: Samba
blurb: Made in 1950 for footballers training on frozen pitches; now the low, narrow everyday shoe.
fit_note: Narrow through the toe. Take your usual size; go up a third if your feet are wide.

name: Handball Spezial
blurb: An indoor handball shoe from 1979, suede and leather on a gum sole.
fit_note: True to size, with a softer, roomier collar than the Samba.

name: Gazelle
blurb: The 1960s training shoe in suede, worn on terraces ever since.
fit_note: True to size. The Indoor version sits a little wider at the toe.

name: Adizero
blurb: adidas's light running shoes, from daily trainers to race-day flats.
fit_note: A snug, race-like fit. Take your usual size, or a third up for long runs.

name: Megaride
blurb: An early-2000s runner with visible cushioning at the heel, back as a statement shoe.
fit_note: True to size, with plenty of cushioning under the heel.
